newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES FORMALLY PROTEST JETER HOME RUN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES FORMALLY PROTEST JETER HOME RUN.

text.p: The Baltimore Orioles on Thursday formally protested Derek Jeter's eighth-inning home run in Game 1 of the American League Championship Series, saying that umpire Rich Garcia was now convinced he had erred in not calling fan interference.

Jeter's homer, deflected by a 12-year-old fan's glove back into the stands as right fielder Tony Tarasco waited to catch it at the wall, tied the game, later won by the Yankees on an 11th-inning homer by Bernie Williams.
Orioles owner Peter Angelos and general manager Patrick Gillick asked acting commissioner Bud Selig to direct American League president Gene Budig to reverse the umpire's decision.

In a five-page letter with appended reprints of various news reports, the Orioles said Budig should "recognize the umpire is now convinced that there was fan interference, and order that the game be re-played from the eighth inning forward. The best interests of baseball demand no less."
The Orioles' protest cited Section 3.11 of the American League Rules and Regulations which says:

"There shall be no appeal from any decision of the umpire on the grounds that he was not correct in his conclusion as to whether a batted ball was fair or foul, a base-runner safe or out, a pitched ball a strike or a ball, or any other play involving accuracy of judgment and no decision rendered by him shall be reversed, except that he be convinced that he is in violation of one of the rules."

It was the exception mentioned in the last phrase upon which the Baltimore club based its right to protest a judgment call, citing news reports that had Garcia acknowledging that upon viewing television replays, he would have called the play differently.

"By his own explanation, Jeter's fly was 'not a home run,' likely a 'missed call,' 'probably interference,' and at most a ball that would have 'only hit the wall,'" said the protest, which included the full news stories in which the Garcia quotes appeared.
